goal: Replace the flat specialist skill lists with a composed, discoverable, DSH-native skill layer: verified frontmatter, layered composition, find-activate-load discovery wired to DSH invalidation, a provider contract reconciled with the merged session-workspace routing fix, a generated package catalog, and verification against a real DeepSeek Harness checkout.

alignment.evidence: Feature branch feature/skill-architecture-v2 rebased onto main 44eb167; Project Harness reusable harness only, no product code and no live DSH session.

Read the DSH skill subsystem doc and source, PR #6, PR #8, the merged regression test and the divergent branch; then executed the provider against DSH's real registry and filesystem provider and diffed our frontmatter parser against DSH's own, which found two real divergences.
00-PLANNING/SKILL-ARCHITECTURE-V2.md models the gap, the composition design, and the reconciliation table mapping each merged PR #8 contract onto this implementation.

Skill layer and adapter only. One bounded write (.harness/state/skills.json on activation). No shell, no Git mutation, no merge, release, deployment or live provider call. The divergent remote branch was left untouched.

DSH owns the registry, layering and catalogue rendering; dsh/skills/*.js owns composition, discovery and workspace resolution; capabilities.json owns the vocabulary; each skill owns its own frontmatter.

Phase one, reconciliation with main, the reviewed merge of the parallel branch's layer vocabulary and catalog validation, plus live integration and YAML-conformance verification against a real DeepSeek Harness checkout. Native .dsh/skills migration, new specialists, and an in-session live model run remain out of scope.

Node built-ins only, no new dependency; bounded walks and reads; path containment on reads and the single write; atomic write; stat-poll instead of a chokidar dependency; stray non-skill entry and duplicate preset filename removed.
